<!-- nexkit:request:maintenance:acceptance-existing-head-health-20260926 -->
<!-- nexkit:pipeline:maintenance -->
## Original request

> Add HEAD /health to the existing Python standard-library label service so clients
> can inspect health response metadata without downloading a response body.
> 
> On the existing loopback listener and CLI-selected port, HEAD /health must return
> HTTP 200 with the same application/json content type and Content-Length value as
> GET /health, and no HTTP response body. GET /health must keep returning the same
> JSON health payload. Preserve the established normalization behavior, unknown GET
> route behavior, CLI startup and deterministic package behavior.
> 
> Add regression coverage using the actual service process and real HTTP requests,
> including a check that distinguishes an empty HEAD response on the wire from a
> client merely hiding a received body. Verify the endpoint from the extracted
> package too. Keep all three configured unit, HTTP and package suites separately
> runnable with useful assertions. Document the endpoint in README.md.
> 
> Keep Python 3.12+ and the standard library. Add no third-party runtime dependency,
> external service or authentication. Do not change NexKit workflows, prompts,
> skills, accepted policy or usage limits. This request does not include a release
> or deployment.
> 
> This is the third and final work item within the owner's previously accepted
> three-item live acceptance scope. Clarify the authoritative specification on the
> GitHub issue and wait for the owner's exact requirement approval before any
> application implementation. Delivery must follow the maintenance pipeline's
> configured human review gate after current checks and independent AI review.
<!-- nexkit:spec -->
Add HEAD /health to the existing Python standard-library label service so clients
can inspect health response metadata without downloading a response body.

On the existing loopback listener and CLI-selected port, HEAD /health must return
HTTP 200 with the same application/json content type and Content-Length value as
GET /health, and no HTTP response body. GET /health must keep returning the same
JSON health payload. Preserve the established normalization behavior, unknown GET
route behavior, CLI startup and deterministic package behavior.

Add regression coverage using the actual service process and real HTTP requests,
including a check that distinguishes an empty HEAD response on the wire from a
client merely hiding a received body. Verify the endpoint from the extracted
package too. Keep all three configured unit, HTTP and package suites separately
runnable with useful assertions. Document the endpoint in README.md.

Keep Python 3.12+ and the standard library. Add no third-party runtime dependency,
external service or authentication. Do not change NexKit workflows, prompts,
skills, accepted policy or usage limits. This request does not include a release
or deployment.

This is the third and final work item within the owner's previously accepted
three-item live acceptance scope. Clarify the authoritative specification on
the GitHub issue and wait for the owner's exact requirement approval before any
application implementation. Delivery must follow the maintenance pipeline's
configured human review gate after current checks and independent AI review.

<!-- nexkit:clarification:4a6a6e72862f05e4ecb449f11b1470f57efae548b9b9e19caa6fbcdea80511b4 -->
The current handler implements GET only. GET /health returns the existing JSON payload and its Content-Type and Content-Length headers. The requested HEAD response and regression criteria are clear, and I found no missing product decision. The specification is ready for your exact requirement approval.

The specification is ready for human review. An authorized human may approve this exact version with:

`/nexkit approve 90e56f84eef49613ceba208d9cff54389efe5b2dedefced337597e01a41e6c2e`
